Every mutation below moves an offset, an argument, an index or an order, and each one has a fixture feature behind it: three distinguishable encoder stubs, a pseudorandom FP block and parameter block, a ring whose rails and `sym` array hold different data, and a cursor seeded at 32767 over a buffer with 32,768 shorts of headroom below it.

the encoder table is read one slot high, which is V17TX_create's abs where it laid dif
the selector is read from the two bytes above it
the selector indexes the table unsigned, which agrees over every value V17TX_create can leave and not over a negative one
the coder and the ring are handed to the encoder the other way round
the coder is taken from the ring's offset, so the encoder is handed the ring twice
the shaper is filtered from a ring that is not the one the encoder wrote
the shaper's count is the number of samples it may write rather than the number of symbols offered
the encoder's count is one short, so the last data word never reaches the ring
the no-carrier symbol comes from two bytes below the field the object reads
the no-carrier symbol comes from two bytes above it

the wrap test is unsigned, which agrees everywhere except at the truncation corner
the next cursor is not truncated to a short, so 32767 does not wrap to -32768
the ring length is read where the read cursor lives
the write cursor is initialised from the read cursor
the write cursor is not written back, so a caller filling the ring across calls overwrites the same slots
the write cursor is written back into the read cursor
